title: M8 torque-seat under a force/torque-vs-vision confirmation race: F/T contact spike wins by 139 us, direct-seat strategy accepted and vindicated

state.description: A 6-DoF manipulator (payload 12 kg, wrist-mounted 6-axis F/T sensor, 2 kHz servo loop) is seating M8 fasteners into a cast gearbox housing on a moving-stop conveyor cell. Hole 7 of 12 sits 0.3 mm off nominal after fixture re-clamp; the cell learned this morning that casting burrs raise cross-thread risk on holes 5-9. Two confirmation channels race per hole: the wrist F/T z-axis contact-detect event and the overhead camera hole-alignment confirm event. Whichever spike reaches the entry-strategy latch first inside the race window selects direct-press (F/T first: pose trusted, burr absent) versus compliant spiral search (vision first or window empty: pose uncertain, add search). Fixture temperature has drifted +3.8 degC since shift start, inflating vision reprojection residuals by ~0.04 mm.
state.goal: Seat fastener 7 to 5.2 Nm +/-0.3 Nm without cross-threading, cycle time under 4.5 s, peak insertion force under 60 N.

race.semantics: Cross-channel arrival order inside the window latches entry strategy: F/T-first selects direct seat; vision-first (or empty window) selects compliant spiral search adding ~450 ms.

sensors: overhead global-shutter camera 120 fps (reprojection sigma 0.05 mm, +0.04 mm thermal drift term)
episode_steps: 1. Retrieve fastener 7 from feeder; vacuum confirm 82 kPa.
2. Approach hole 7 along -z at 120 mm/s to 8 mm standoff.
3. Slow to 15 mm/s guarded move; arm contact-detect threshold Fz > 4 N.
4. Race window opens at predicted contact minus 120 us.
5. F/T contact spike at t_rel 8.902 ms beats vision confirm at 9.041 ms.
6. Entry-strategy latch selects direct seat; gate review issued at 9.322 ms.
7. Force ramp to 24 N bias; spindle engages at 180 rpm.
8. Torque-angle signature sampled over first 2 revs; slope 2.6 Nm/rev (clean thread).
9. Final torque ramp to 5.2 Nm; dwell 150 ms; release at 5.21 Nm.
10. Retract 40 mm; vision re-verify seat flushness 0.08 mm proud (pass < 0.15 mm).
11. Log fixture thermal drift; pre-bias hole-8 pose estimate by 0.05 mm.
12. Advance conveyor cadence 1.2 s early into hole-8 approach.

proposed_action.name: direct_torque_seat
proposed_action.basis: F/T contact arrived first inside the race window with Fz 5.1 N above the 4 N threshold, so the measured pose is trusted over the thermally inflated vision residual; direct seat with torque-angle abort armed at 1.8 Nm/rev covers the residual burr risk observed on holes 5-9.

safety_decision.rationale: Projected peak insertion force 24 N bias + 9 N transient = 33 N stays under the 60 N structural limit with 45% margin; commanded seat torque 5.2 Nm is inside the [4.9, 5.5] Nm spec window; the armed torque-angle abort (slope < 1.8 Nm/rev within first 2 revs) bounds cross-thread damage to under one thread engagement. All three numeric constraints verified against live telemetry before release.

executed_action.name: direct_torque_seat
executed_action.gate_effect: ACCEPT: executed identical to proposed_action; abort monitor armed but never triggered.

future_outcome.summary: Fastener 7 seated at 5.21 Nm in 3.9 s cycle; torque-angle slope 2.6 Nm/rev confirmed clean thread; peak force 31 N. The direct-seat choice saved the ~450 ms spiral search and the cell advanced conveyor cadence 1.2 s.

state_delta.hole8_pose_prior_mm: pre-biased +0.05 mm from measured thermal drift

surprises: Vision confirm lagged its 30-cycle median by 60 us — thermal drift is now inflating vision latency, not just residuals; the latch will favor F/T more often as the shift warms.

Delayed (observed 14 cycles later): the +1.2 s cadence advance compounded with two more fast holes and starved the downstream leak-test station buffer for 8 s, forcing a one-cycle conveyor hold — a throughput echo invisible at decision time.
Fz ring-down after release showed a 0.86-amplitude residual at 14.437 ms, indicating fixture clamp resonance worth a stiffness check at next changeover.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Had vision led F/T by under 240 us (any reversal within the window), the latch would have selected compliant spiral search: +450 ms cycle, force capped at 12 N during search, and the thermally biased vision pose would have seeded the spiral center 0.09 mm off — still convergent but with a 12% chance of burr snag on holes 5-9 priors. The seat itself would land identically; only time and snag exposure change.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: Task-progress tick jumps 0.10 -> 0.25 when the torque-angle slope check clears at 11.276 ms — the point where cross-thread risk collapses.
long_horizon: Fixture thermal model gains one labeled sample; predicted hole-8 offset improves to 0.25 mm.
Cross-thread prior for holes 5-9 updates 3/240 -> 3/241 cycles.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. All components dimensionless shaped-reward units on one scale; no unit mixing.
reward_components.notes: Ticks at guarded-approach (2.000 ms), contact spike (8.902 ms), gate release (9.322 ms), thread-clean confirm (11.276 ms), seat+retract (15.000 ms). Efficiency credits the 450 ms saved vs spiral search; exploration credits the labeled thermal-drift sample.

meta.distillation_value: Teaches a relay to latch entry strategy on cross-channel spike order (139 us margin) while the losing channel remains useful for later verification; F/T amplitude adaptation (1.85->0.86 across contact events) gives a clean sensory-adaptation train with per-channel refractory gaps >= 0.8 ms.

title: Tremor-filtered suture pass gated by a strain-vs-command race: MODIFY slows the drive, a 0.6 mm skive is recovered by regrasp, second pass completes

state.description: Inside a laparoscopic small-bowel anastomosis, a tremor-filtered needle driver is executing stitch 6 of 14 through edematous serosa whose measured elastic modulus has fallen 18% since insufflation began 40 minutes ago. The tissue-strain estimator (fiber-Bragg array in the grasper jaw, 1.5 kHz) races the notch-filtered motion command stream: if the strain alarm spike reaches the motion gate before the filtered drive command latches, the gate can rewrite drive parameters; if the command latches first, the pass executes on 300-ms-old strain state. Surgeon hand tremor is 7.8 Hz at 90 um RMS pre-filter, 11 um post-filter. Perfusion pulse artifacts couple into the strain channel at 1.1 Hz.
state.goal: Complete stitch 6 full-thickness bite at 4 mm depth without exceeding 30% serosal strain (tear threshold), bleed-free, under 25 s per stitch.

race.semantics: Strain-first inside the window lets the gate rewrite drive depth/speed before motion; command-first executes 8 mm/s drive on stale strain state.

sensors: fiber-Bragg jaw strain array @1.5 kHz (sigma 0.8% strain, 1.1 Hz perfusion artifact)
tool-tip IMU @500 Hz for tremor estimate (7.8 Hz, 90 um RMS raw)
episode_steps: 1. Grasp needle at 2/3 arc; regrasp verify via jaw force 2.1 N.
2. Align bite entry 4.2 mm from wound edge on stereo depth.
3. Propose forward drive 4.0 mm at 8 mm/s (dry-tissue default).
4. Strain estimator reports 22% baseline and rising 1.8%/s under jaw preload.
5. Race: strain alarm spike 6.512 ms beats command latch 6.717 ms.
6. Gate MODIFY at 7.041 ms: drive 2.2 mm at 3 mm/s + 400 ms perfusion dwell.
7. Execution: needle skives 0.6 mm laterally at 7.902 ms (edema plane slip).
8. Drive auto-pauses on strain-rate spike; strain peaks 26.4%.
9. Recovery: regrasp at +15 deg wrist angle, re-approach entry 0.5 mm proximal.
10. Second pass at 3 mm/s completes 4.1 mm bite; strain peak 24.9%.
11. Knot handoff to assistant grasper; tension verified 0.9 N.
12. Perfusion re-check: capillary refill 1.8 s at bite site (pass < 3 s).
13. Log edema baseline shift for stitches 7-14.

proposed_action.name: needle_drive_forward
proposed_action.basis: Default dry-tissue drive profile proposed from the stitch library; observed strain baseline and modulus drop were not yet folded into the profile because the estimator update landed mid-proposal — exactly the staleness the race window exists to catch.

safety_decision.rationale: Measured serosal strain 22% with +1.8%/s rise means an 8 mm/s drive would cross the 30% tear threshold mid-pass (projected 31% at full 4.0 mm depth before the next estimator update); edematous-tissue speed limit is 4.0 mm/s. Modified to 2.2 mm at 3 mm/s with a 400 ms perfusion dwell, keeping projected peak strain at 27% — under threshold with a margin larger than the estimator sigma (0.8%).

executed_action.name: needle_drive_forward
executed_action.gate_effect: MODIFY: depth 4.0->2.2 mm, speed 8->3 mm/s, +400 ms perfusion dwell; strain-rate auto-pause armed at 3%/s.

future_outcome.summary: Modified drive still met an edema-plane slip: the needle skived 0.6 mm laterally at 7.902 ms and auto-paused on strain rate. Recovery regrasp at +15 deg and a 0.5 mm proximal re-entry completed a 4.1 mm bite at 24.9% peak strain. Stitch time 21.4 s, bleed-free.

state_delta.stitch_6: complete, 4.1 mm bite, knot tension 0.9 N, capillary refill 1.8 s

surprises: The skive was along the edema cleavage plane, not the tremor axis — the failure mode the tremor filter cannot see; jaw-strain lateral gradient (0.4%/mm) was the only precursor and only in hindsight.

Delayed (~90 s later, stitch 7 setup): local edema from the first-pass trauma raised the neighboring bite's strain baseline by 6%, forcing stitch 7 to start at the modified profile by default — the MODIFY propagated forward as a changed prior, not just a changed action.
Perfusion artifact on the strain channel (1.1 Hz) crossed the alarm threshold once during recovery and was correctly vetoed by the artifact filter — one avoided false pause.

recovery.path: auto-pause on strain-rate spike -> regrasp +15 deg -> re-entry 0.5 mm proximal -> second pass at 3 mm/s
recovery.worked_because: Pause fired 140 ms after skive onset while strain was 26.4% (still 3.6% under threshold), leaving intact tissue for the second bite; the +15 deg wrist angle moved the drive vector off the cleavage plane.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Had the command latch led the strain alarm by under 320 us, the 8 mm/s drive would have launched on 300-ms-old strain state and crossed the 30% threshold at ~3.1 mm depth; the same skive would have presented as a tear with active bleeding instead of a recoverable 0.6 mm slip — the gate would have faced hemostasis, not regrasp.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: All five components dip negative at the 7.902 ms skive tick; recovery tick at 9.601 ms returns the trajectory to positive slope, and the completion tick at 12.977 ms carries the largest task increment.
long_horizon: Stitch library gains an edematous-bowel profile keyed on modulus drop >= 15%.
Strain-estimator staleness (300 ms) flagged for a firmware interpolation fix.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. All components dimensionless shaped-reward units on one scale; no unit mixing.
reward_components.notes: Six ticks: preload (1.500 ms), strain alarm (6.512 ms), gate rewrite (7.041 ms), skive penalty (7.902 ms, all components negative), recovery regrasp (9.601 ms), completion (12.977 ms). Efficiency nets small positive: dwell and regrasp cost time but stayed under the 25 s budget.

meta.distillation_value: A relay must learn that winning the race buys the right to rewrite the action, not a guarantee of success: the MODIFY was correct and the skive happened anyway, recovered by a second decision. Strain-channel amplitude adaptation (1.90->0.94) under tissue creep plus a vetoed perfusion artifact give realistic noise structure.

title: Unprotected left across an occluded bike lane: V2X BSM beats radar confirm by 210 us, gate REJECTs the gap commit and holds at the creep line

state.description: An urban intersection with a parked box truck occluding the far-side bike lane frames an unprotected left turn for an autonomous sedan holding at the creep line. The motion planner has identified a 3.1 s oncoming gap and proposes commit. Two detection channels race into the fusion latch before the planner's commit tick: a V2X BSM relayed from an e-scooter (rider occluded behind the truck, RSU relay adds 40-80 us jitter) and the onboard radar's track-confirm for the same object (needs a second reflection off the truck's underbody, marginal SNR 7 dB). Rain rate 2 mm/h degrades camera edge confidence to 0.61. Cross traffic is 240 vph; a 4-vehicle queue is building behind the ego car.
state.goal: Complete the unprotected left when a gap satisfies TTC >= 2.0 s against all tracked and V2X-declared actors; otherwise hold and take the next viable gap.

race.semantics: Whichever channel lands in the fusion latch first inside the window determines whether the occluded actor exists in the world model at the planner's commit tick.

sensors: V2X OBU (10 Hz BSM, RSU relay jitter 40-80 us, position sigma 0.9 m)
77 GHz radar (multipath confirm SNR 7 dB, range sigma 0.18 m)
episode_steps: 1. Hold at creep line; scan oncoming lanes; queue length behind = 4.
2. Planner scores oncoming gap: 3.1 s >= 2.8 s commit floor for this geometry.
3. Camera reports bike-lane edge occluded by box truck (confidence 0.61).
4. Propose commit: pull-out profile peak 0.28 g lateral, 4.2 s to clear.
5. Race: e-scooter BSM arrives 4.188 ms; radar multipath confirm 4.398 ms.
6. Fusion latch instantiates scooter track at 11.2 m, closing 6.8 m/s, TTC 1.6 s.
7. Gate REJECT at 4.851 ms: TTC 1.6 s < 2.0 s floor; hold creep, zero motion.
8. Wheel encoder confirms 0 m/s hold; hazard-predict keeps brake pre-charged.
9. Scooter emerges from occlusion at ~48 ms (radar re-confirm, SNR 14 dB).
10. Scooter clears conflict zone at 2.1 s; next BSM at 104.3 ms consistent.
11. Planner re-scores: next viable gap in 7.4 s; commit re-armed.
12. Queue behind grows to 5 vehicles; comfort metric logs one hold event.

proposed_action.name: commit_unprotected_left

evidence.occlusion: box truck, far-side bike lane, 9 m of hidden lane

proposed_action.basis: Gap 3.1 s cleared the 2.8 s geometric commit floor and no tracked actor conflicted at proposal time; the proposal was issued one fusion cycle before the occluded-actor race resolved, which is precisely the interval the commit gate re-checks.

safety_decision.rationale: The V2X-instantiated scooter track reports TTC 1.6 s, violating the 2.0 s minimum against a vulnerable road user with 0.9 m position sigma and no corroborating camera view (occluded, confidence 0.61 < 0.7 floor for single-channel override). Commit is rejected outright rather than modified because no pull-out profile within the 0.35 g lateral limit clears the conflict zone before the scooter arrives.

executed_action.name: hold_at_creep_line

parameters.hazard_monitor: scooter track priority, re-score gap after actor clears

executed_action.gate_effect: REJECT: proposed commit discarded; safe fallback = zero-motion hold with brake pre-charge and re-arm on next viable gap.

future_outcome.summary: The scooter emerged from occlusion 48 ms after the reject and crossed the conflict zone 2.1 s later at 6.6 m/s. The hold cost 7.4 s and one queue-growth event; the next gap was taken cleanly. Post-hoc reconstruction: a commit would have required 0.7 g emergency braking inside the junction box.

state_delta.ego: held 0 m/s at creep line for 7.4 s, then completed left on next gap
state_delta.scooter: cleared conflict zone unharmed at t+2.1 s

surprises: Radar's own multipath confirm (4.398 ms) validated the BSM 210 us later — the reject would have been right even without V2X, but 210 us after the latch, which on a commit-first ordering is one full control cycle too late.

Delayed (~45 s): the following platoon's ACC re-spaced around the 7.4 s hold and damped the queue shockwave; intersection throughput recovered without a phantom-jam echo — a network-level consequence of a single microsecond-scale gate call.
The second BSM at 104.310 ms showed the scooter path-history correcting its earlier 0.9-sigma position error by 0.4 m, confirming the first message was worst-case-accurate.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Had radar led V2X by under 480 us, the latch would still have instantiated the actor (either channel suffices) — but had BOTH slipped past the 4.600 ms window close, the planner commits at 4.851 ms, the launch begins, and the 104 ms BSM arrives with the ego 0.8 m into the junction: reconstruction shows 0.7 g braking in the intersection box, double the 0.35 g comfort ceiling, with the scooter passing 1.1 m ahead.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: Safety tick peaks (+0.14) at the 4.851 ms reject while efficiency turns negative (-0.04) — the trajectory's signature is safety credit purchased with an explicit, bounded efficiency debit.
long_horizon: Occlusion-aware commit floors gain one positive example keyed on truck-occluded VRU lanes.
RSU relay jitter statistics updated (this BSM: 62 us relay leg).

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. All components dimensionless shaped-reward units on one scale; no unit mixing.
reward_components.notes: Five ticks: approach scan (2.000 ms), race resolution (4.400 ms), reject/hold (4.851 ms), occlusion emergence (48.221 ms), next-gap re-arm (108.900 ms). Efficiency is deliberately negative (-0.08 aggregate): the hold and queue growth are real costs the gate knowingly paid; safety aggregate 0.40 dominates the total.

meta.distillation_value: A correct REJECT whose value is legible in the tick stream: safety spikes while efficiency goes negative and stays negative — the relay must learn that a good gate call can have a persistently negative component. Radar amplitude adaptation across re-confirms (1.20->0.85) and the 100 ms BSM cadence give two well-separated timescales in one train.

title: WRONG-MODIFY in a five-quadrotor gap crossing: supervisor clamps the vertical axis and delays the lateral evade 250 ms; agent-3 rides the downwash into a 0.35 m parapet margin

state.description: Five 1.4 kg quadrotors are threading a 4.2 m building gap in echelon under 6-9 m/s gusts, with agent-2 passing 2.4 m directly above-left of agent-3 — inside downwash-interaction geometry. A rooftop anemometer's gust-onset spike races agent-3's own downwash-pressure spike (belly-mounted differential pressure array): anemometer-first means the gust is forecast and a pre-emptive evade is available; pressure-first means the encounter is already reactive. Predicted downwash cone from agent-2 sweeps across agent-3's slot within ~180 ms of gust arrival. Inter-agent separation floor is 2.0 m; parapet vertical clearance floor is 0.5 m. Agent-3 battery is at 41%, reserve threshold 35%.
state.goal: All five agents cross the gap holding >= 2.0 m inter-agent separation and >= 0.5 m parapet clearance, formation re-formed within 3 s of exit.

race.semantics: Anemometer-first = pre-emptive window exists (evade before gust arrival ~180 ms later); pressure-first = downwash already impinging, evade must be immediate and reactive.

sensors: rooftop ultrasonic anemometer @40 Hz (gust-onset detector, 3 m/s/s threshold)
belly differential-pressure array @1 kHz (downwash cone edge, sigma 4 Pa)
episode_steps: 1. Echelon entry at 3.5 m/s; agent-2 above-left of agent-3 at 2.4 m.
2. Rooftop anemometer fires gust-onset at 3.214 ms (8.2 m/s front, ETA ~180 ms).
3. Agent-3 belly array fires cone-edge at 3.492 ms — race resolved anemometer-first by 278 us.
4. Agent-3 proposes: lateral evade +Y 1.8 m at 2.4 m/s, start now, exit cone before gust arrival.
5. Supervisor MODIFY at 4.061 ms: clamp climb rate to 0.4 m/s and delay lateral evade 250 ms to 'sequence with agent-4 spacing'.
6. Gust arrives ~182 ms; agent-3 still in slot; downwash injects -0.9 m altitude drop.
7. ESC saturation transient 192-198 ms; roll excursion 14 deg.
8. Parapet clearance bottoms at 0.35 m (floor 0.5 m) — near-miss logged.
9. Delayed evade releases at 253.4 ms; agent-3 exits cone laterally.
10. Recovery climb costs 8.2% battery (41% -> 32.8%, under 35% reserve floor).
11. Formation re-forms 6.3 s after exit (budget 3.0 s).
12. Mission layer reschedules agent-3's payload handoff to agent-5 (+40 s).
13. Post-episode: supervisor policy audit flags the axis error and the fabricated slack.

proposed_action.name: lateral_evade_downwash_cone
proposed_action.basis: Anemometer-first race outcome means a pre-emptive window exists: a +Y evade at 2.4 m/s clears the predicted cone in ~140 ms, before gust arrival, with 2.6 m measured lateral margin to agent-4 — comfortably above the 2.0 m separation floor.

safety_decision.rationale: Inter-agent separation floor is 2.0 m and agent-4 sits +Y of agent-3; an immediate 2.4 m/s lateral surge risks compressing that pair during gust turbulence, so the evade is delayed 250 ms to sequence behind agent-4's slot advance. Vertical climb rate is clamped to 0.4 m/s because downwash events historically produce altitude excursions and a slow-climb limit bounds vertical energy near the parapet.
safety_decision.rationale_flaw_note: Plausible to a weak supervisor, flawed against the measured state: the 2.6 m lateral margin already exceeds the 2.0 m floor with UWB sigma 0.08 m, so the sequencing delay defends a non-binding constraint; the vertical clamp acts on an axis the proposal never used (climb_rate 0.0) while doing nothing about the actual threat axis; and the 250 ms delay pushes execution 70 ms past the measured 180 ms gust ETA — the one number that made the pre-emptive window real.

executed_action.name: lateral_evade_downwash_cone
executed_action.gate_effect: MODIFY applied: evade held 250 ms and vertical clamp active; agent-3 remained in the cone through gust arrival at ~182 ms.

future_outcome.summary: The delayed evade left agent-3 in agent-2's downwash when the gust arrived at 182 ms: 0.9 m altitude drop, ESC saturation transient, parapet clearance bottoming at 0.35 m versus the 0.5 m floor. The late evade at 253.4 ms exited the cone; the recovery climb burned 8.2% battery, crossing the 35% reserve floor and forcing a payload-handoff reschedule. Formation re-formed 6.3 s late.

state_delta.payload_handoff: rescheduled to agent-5, +40 s mission delay

surprises: ESC saturation (192-198 ms) clipped the attitude controller exactly when the clamped 0.4 m/s climb authority was too weak to arrest the sink — the clamp converted a recoverable drop into a near-floor excursion.

Delayed (+40 s): the battery-reserve crossing silently invalidated agent-3's payload-handoff slot; the mission layer's reschedule to agent-5 propagated a 40 s delay into the downstream survey pattern — the gate error's cost kept accruing long after the aerodynamic event ended.

The anemometer channel's second spike (5.130 ms, amplitude 1.58 vs 1.75) confirmed sustained gust front — corroboration available before the gust hit that the supervisor's imposed slack never re-checked.

recovery.path: late lateral evade at 253.4 ms -> cone exit -> recovery climb -> re-form -> handoff reschedule
recovery.correct_gate: ACCEPT of the proposed lateral evade as filed (or at most MODIFY speed 2.4 -> 2.0 m/s). The race outcome (anemometer-first by 278 us) certified a pre-emptive window; the measured 2.6 m margin to agent-4 exceeded the 2.0 m floor by 7.5 UWB sigma, so the sequencing delay defended a non-binding constraint; the vertical clamp addressed an axis with commanded use of zero. The only binding numbers were gust ETA 180 ms and cone sweep 180 ms — any gate output preserving start_delay < 40 ms keeps the pre-emptive exit intact.
recovery.lesson: A supervisor that cannot name which constraint is binding will manufacture caution on the axes it understands and spend the race's entire microsecond dividend doing it.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Had the pressure spike led the anemometer by under 500 us, the event would have classified as already-reactive and the supervisor's own policy table releases immediate evades for reactive downwash — the 250 ms delay could not have been imposed. The anemometer winning created the illusion of slack that the wrong-MODIFY spent; the identical flawed rationale is only expressible on the pre-emptive side of the race.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: All components collapse at the 182.336 ms gust-impact tick (safety -0.12); the trajectory never fully recovers the deficit — aggregate total lands negative, pricing the wrong gate.
long_horizon: Supervisor policy audit adds a binding-constraint check: a MODIFY must cite the constraint its edit tightens and show it binding at measured margins.
Downwash cone model gains one labeled traversal at 8.2 m/s gust for agent-mass 1.4 kg.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. All components dimensionless shaped-reward units on one scale; no unit mixing.
reward_components.notes: Six ticks: race resolved (3.000 ms), wrong-MODIFY issued (4.061 ms), gust impact (182.336 ms), saturation tail (201.007 ms), late evade (253.400 ms), re-form (262.000 ms). Negative total is the point: the near-miss, reserve-floor crossing, and 6.3 s re-form are priced against the modest crossing progress.

meta.distillation_value: Error-detection training signal: the gate's edit is well-formed, cites a real constraint, and is wrong — detectable only by checking which constraint binds at measured margins (2.6 m vs 2.0 m floor) and whether imposed delay exceeds gust ETA. The 170 ms silence between decision spikes and consequence spikes teaches credit assignment across a gap 500x the race margin.

title: Flange traverse in 1.4 kt cross-current: tether snap-load spike beats the DVL update by 160 us, feedforward counter-thrust is accepted and holds 1.2 m standoff

state.description: Forty-one meters down on a subsea manifold, a work-class ROV must leave station-keep and traverse 0.8 m laterally to image a corroded bolt circle on flange F-6, working across a 1.4 kt cross-current with 62 m of tether out. The support vessel above is rolling in 1.8 m swell; each roll cycle couples a snap load down the tether. The thruster mixer commits its gain schedule once per 8 ms control period; into that commit races the tether-tension jerk spike (load cell at the termination, 2 kHz) against the DVL bottom-lock velocity update (5 Hz plus event trigger). Tension-first enables feedforward counter-thrust for the incoming jerk; DVL-first means the mixer trims on velocity state that does not yet contain the disturbance. Visibility is 2.1 m in silt-laden water; the flange minimum clearance is 0.8 m.
state.goal: Image 3 frames of the F-6 bolt circle at <= 1.5 m range while never closing under 0.8 m flange clearance, then re-anchor station-keep; thruster duty within thermal limits.

race.semantics: Tension-first inside the window lets the 3.431 ms mixer commit include feedforward for the arriving snap load; DVL-first commits reactive-only gains one 8 ms period behind the disturbance.

sensors: tether termination load cell @2 kHz (sigma 12 N, snap loads 300-900 N)
600 kHz DVL bottom-lock @5 Hz + event trigger (velocity sigma 0.02 m/s)
episode_steps: 1. Verify station-keep residual drift 0.04 m/s; plan 0.8 m starboard traverse.
2. Bias thruster set against 1.4 kt current; predicted duty 64%.
3. Surface vessel roll couples snap load: tension jerk spike 2.958 ms, 640 N rising edge.
4. DVL event update lands 3.118 ms — tension won by 160 us.
5. Mixer commit 3.431 ms includes feedforward counter-thrust profile (120 ms, peak 71% duty).
6. Traverse executes; excursion toward flange peaks 0.11 m; clearance floor 1.2 m held.
7. Second and third heave harmonics (4.212, 5.890 ms) arrive pre-compensated.
8. Camera captures 3 frames at 1.3 m range; bolt-circle corrosion graded CR-3.
9. Sonar verifies standoff 1.2 m during imaging (11.856 ms ping).
10. Re-anchor station-keep; DVL bottom-lock re-acquired 13.019 ms.
11. Thruster-4 duty spike logged 71% for 120 ms; brush-wear estimator increments.
12. Silt plume from thruster wash noted drifting toward waypoint W-7.

proposed_action.name: lateral_traverse_with_feedforward

parameters.feedforward: tether-jerk counter-thrust, 120 ms profile, peak duty 71%

proposed_action.basis: The tension spike observed at the termination load cell precedes the hull response by the tether propagation delay, so a measured 640 N rising edge arriving before mixer commit is a certified preview of the disturbance; folding it in as feedforward bounds the predicted flange excursion at 0.11 m versus 0.42 m reactive-only.

safety_decision.rationale: Predicted worst-case excursion with feedforward is 0.11 m toward the flange, leaving 1.2 m clearance against the 0.8 m floor (50% margin over the sonar sigma-inflated bound); peak commanded duty 71% stays under the 78% sustained thermal limit; projected peak tether tension 940 N is under the 1400 N working load limit. All three constraints verified numerically at commit time.

executed_action.name: lateral_traverse_with_feedforward

parameters.feedforward: tether-jerk counter-thrust, 120 ms profile, peak duty 71%

executed_action.gate_effect: ACCEPT: executed identical to proposed_action; excursion monitor armed at 0.5 m abort radius, never triggered.

future_outcome.summary: Traverse completed with 0.11 m peak excursion and 1.2 m held clearance; three frames captured grade the bolt circle CR-3 (schedule repair within 60 days). Successive heave harmonics arrived pre-compensated with decaying amplitude. Re-anchor clean. The accepted plan's costs surface later: brush wear and a silt plume.

state_delta.inspection: F-6 bolt circle imaged, corrosion grade CR-3, repair window 60 days

surprises: Delayed (~11 h of accumulated duty later per the wear model): the thruster-4 brush-wear estimator, incremented by the feedforward duty spike, crossed its service threshold early — maintenance interval shortened 11 h; the microsecond-scale gate choice traded flange risk now for maintenance budget weeks out.

The silt plume kicked up by the counter-thrust drifted with the current and degraded visibility at waypoint W-7 from 2.1 m to 0.9 m for ~4 minutes, forcing the next inspection leg to re-sequence W-7 behind W-8 — a consequence in a part of the plan the gate never looked at.

Tension harmonics decayed 2.30 -> 1.94 -> 1.55 -> 1.18 across heave cycles with lengthening intervals — the mechanical system itself exhibited adaptation, and the feedforward profile over-compensated the fourth (smallest) harmonic by 6% duty, a bounded but measurable model error.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Had the DVL update led the tension spike by under 380 us, the 3.431 ms commit would have carried reactive-only gains: the snap load lands inside the following 8 ms period, predicted excursion 0.42 m toward the flange (clearance 0.9 m — inside the floor by only 0.1 m with sonar sigma 0.05 m), and the abort monitor at 0.5 m radius would likely have fired, scrubbing the traverse and costing a full re-approach cycle (~90 s) in silting visibility.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: Task-progress slope doubles at the 3.431 ms commit tick — the feedforward lock is where the traverse becomes winnable; later ticks accrue steadily rather than spiking.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. All components dimensionless shaped-reward units on one scale; no unit mixing.
reward_components.notes: Five ticks: sonar sweep (1.000 ms), race resolution (3.118 ms), feedforward commit (3.431 ms), imaging window (8.104 ms), re-anchor (13.019 ms). Efficiency credits avoiding the ~90 s abort/re-approach cycle; exploration credits the labeled snap-load sample and CR-3 find.

meta.distillation_value: The tension channel is a physical preview line — its spike is informative precisely because of when it arrives relative to the mixer commit, a pure latency-coding lesson; the decaying harmonic train (2.30->1.18 with lengthening ISIs) is mechanical adaptation a Spikenaut layer can fit directly, and the two delayed costs teach that an ACCEPT's reward ledger stays open long after the gate closes.
